title: Changelog
text:
The multidim path now carries the metadata a writer needs to reproduce the source. Found by round-tripping a multidim VRT of GHRSST MUR COGs through gdalxarray into a VRT writer:

CRS: each array’s GetSpatialRef() is attached the way the classic path does it (an xproj CRSIndex on a scalar crs coordinate), plus a CF crs_wkt attribute on that coordinate and grid_mapping="crs" on the data variables. Previously the multidim path dropped the CRS.
Time encoding: decoded time coordinates keep units, calendar and the stored dtype in .encoding, as xarray’s own decoder does.
Units: GetUnit() reaches attrs["units"] on data variables and non-time coordinates (it was read only to decode time).
Dimension types: GDAL’s HORIZONTAL_X / HORIZONTAL_Y / VERTICAL / TEMPORAL become CF axis X / Y / Z / T on the index coordinates.






CF-1.8 geometry containers now reach xarray in the multidim path, so a vector data cube stored in netCDF decodes with ds.xvec.decode_cf() (#11). GDAL hides 0-d arrays from its multidim listing; containers (0-d arrays with a geometry_type attribute) are now added back, while other hidden arrays such as grid-mapping variables stay hidden. The geometry dimension named by the container’s variable_name no longer gets a placeholder 0..n index, which blocked decoding. Each container gets a grid_mapping pointing at a 0-d crs_wkt coordinate built from the SRS GDAL reports, so the decoded GeometryIndex carries the CRS. Files without geometry containers are unchanged.





Sparse selections on the multidim path read only what they select. The multidim array now declares IndexingSupport.OUTER, so an integer or boolean indexer such as isel(time=(t.month == 6) & (t.day == 27)) reaches the backend instead of being widened by xarray to one covering slab from the first selected index to the last. The backend groups the selected indices into runs (adjacent indices, or indices in the same storage block along that axis), makes one read per run, and restores order and duplicates afterwards. Over a daily mosaic, one day a year for 45 years is now 45 reads rather than every day in between; this is the case that stalled the docs build. Selections with several array axes are capped at GDALMultiDimArray.MAX_OUTER_READS (512) reads, by collapsing the busiest axes to a covering read. Classic-raster paths are unchanged (band lists were already read natively). The dask path is unchanged.








Declared dtypes now match what GDAL returns. Int8, Int64, UInt64 and Float16 bands/arrays were previously declared as float32 while reads returned the native type; the mapping now mirrors osgeo.gdal_array’s.
A multiband raster whose bands all use NaN as nodata is no longer reported as having heterogeneous nodata (NaN != NaN made every band look different), so it decodes normally instead of warning and staying raw.
Classic-raster backend arrays (GDALBackendArray, GDALMultiBandArray) now pickle, dropping per-thread handles and reopening lazily, as the multidim class already did. Before this, multidim=False opens could not be shipped to distributed workers.
With band_as_dim=False, each band variable’s preferred_chunks now uses that band’s own block size rather than band 1’s.





LICENSE now holds the full Apache-2.0 text; the copyright notice moved to NOTICE.
INSTALL: example environment updated to python>=3.11; the osgeo/gdal venv recipe now uses --system-site-packages; added a note that the GDAL bindings must be built against numpy 2.








open_dataset(..., config_options={...}) surfaces GDAL configuration options (#25), e.g. {"GDAL_HTTP_MAX_RETRY": "3"}. Options are applied thread-locally around the open and re-entered around every read, then unset again: per-thread reopens under dask (#34) and reads on distributed workers after unpickling inherit them by construction, and concurrent opens with different options never interfere or leak into unrelated work sharing a thread pool. Values are stringified, the options participate in dask tokenization both on the raw backend arrays and in the managed-chunking layer token (same dsn with different options yields different layer names, so dask never deduplicates across differently-configured opens), and they are not applied during engine auto-detection (guess_can_open). warp() is unchanged; passing options there is a possible follow-up.





Outer and boolean indexers now work on all read paths, and stepped or reversed slices return correct data. Selections built from integer or boolean arrays, e.g. isel(time=(ds.time.dt.month == 6) & (ds.time.dt.day == 27)), previously raised IndexError: Unsupported index type: <class 'numpy.ndarray'>; the three BackendArray classes now declare IndexingSupport.BASIC via xarray’s explicit_indexing_adapter, which decomposes fancy indexers into a covering basic read plus an in-memory numpy step. At the same time the basic reads themselves were completed: the classic-raster paths previously ignored slice steps entirely (a stepped isel returned the wrong shape or wrong rows), every path read negative-step slices forward without reversing the result, and a reversed band slice (isel(band=slice(None, None, -1))) silently returned an empty array. Classic paths serve stepped/reversed slices by reading the smallest contiguous covering window and reordering in numpy; the multidim path keeps native strided reads and flips negative-step axes after the read; band lists pass arbitrary order natively. Negative integer indices are also supported everywhere, raw int/slice keys on the backend arrays keep working (wrapped as BasicIndexer), and the eager coordinate load at open time goes through the raw read path. (Empty integer-array indexers remain an upstream xarray limitation: _decompose_outer_indexer crashes before backend code runs.)
The multidim path is now safe under dask’s threaded scheduler (#34). GDALMultiDimArray previously read through a single shared mdarray handle from every dask worker thread; GDAL handles are not thread-safe per-handle, so threaded computes over chunked multidim data were a data race (crash or corruption). Reads now resolve a per-thread handle lazily (gdal.OpenEx + OpenMDArrayFromFullname per worker thread), the same pattern the classic-raster classes already used: GDAL is thread-safe across handles, drivers take their own global locks internally, and osgeo releases the GIL during I/O, so threaded reads are both safe and genuinely parallel. The constructing thread reuses the already-open handle, so the non-dask path pays no reopen cost. __dask_tokenize__ no longer touches a live handle (it can be called from any thread), and instances now pickle by dropping handles and reopening on first read, which makes the multidim path usable under distributed schedulers.
Empty label selections no longer raise or silently return wrong data (#32). pandas emits positional slices with stop < start and a positive step for an empty label selection on a descending coordinate, e.g. sel(latitude=slice(-16.93, -16.87)) on a north-up grid. All three BackendArray classes previously “flipped” such slices into forward reads: when the flipped window fell out of bounds GDAL raised RuntimeError: arrayStartIdx + (count-1) * arrayStep >= size, and when it stayed in bounds the read silently returned real data for a selection that should be empty. Slices that are empty under Python slice semantics now return correctly shaped zero-size arrays without touching GDAL. (A reverse read is expressed as step < 0, never as stop < start with a positive step.)
A leading ~ in plain filesystem paths is now expanded (#33). GDAL does not perform tilde expansion, so ~/file.tif previously failed with a misleading “not recognized as a supported file format” error. Expansion applies in open_dataset, in guess_can_open (so engine auto-detection also works for ~ paths), and in warp(). Only os.path.expanduser is applied, and only to strings starting with ~: abspath/normpath are deliberately avoided because they corrupt GDAL URIs such as /vsicurl/https://... (collapsing the double slash) and ZARR:/NETCDF: connection strings. All other dsns pass through byte-identical.
The mask_and_scale keyword is now honoured (#29). It was previously accepted by open_dataset and silently ignored; mask_and_scale=False now returns raw values with the CF attributes (scale_factor, add_offset, _FillValue) left in attrs, in both classic layouts and multidim mode.
Unscaled data keeps its native dtype (#29). The band_as_dim=False path previously attached identity scale_factor=1.0 and add_offset=0.0 to every variable (GDAL’s Python bindings return 1.0/0.0 for unset scale/offset), which made CF decoding promote plain unscaled Byte/Int16 imagery to float64. Only informative values are recorded now.
Bands with heterogeneous scale/offset/nodata are surfaced honestly (#29). With band_as_dim=True, per-band values were previously exposed as coordinates named scale_factor/add_offset/_FillValue, names CF decoding cannot consume on a per-band coordinate: the dataset looked decoded while the values stayed raw. Such values are now provided as band_scale_factor/band_add_offset/band_nodata coordinates with a UserWarning pointing at band_as_dim=False, which decodes each band independently. Attributes that are homogeneous across bands still decode (a shared nodata masks even when scales differ).
Breaking for users reading the old per-band coordinate names scale_factor/add_offset/_FillValue on mixed-band datasets.
CF decoding (scale_factor, add_offset, _FillValue) now applies automatically when reading. Previously gdalxarray exposed GDAL’s scale/offset/nodata under non-CF attribute names, which prevented xarray’s CF decoder from applying value transformation and fill-value masking. The result was raw integer values and sentinel-valued land pixels in scaled scientific data (OISST, CMEMS, ERA5, etc.) — silently wrong. The fix renames attributes to CF-standard names in both classic-raster and multidim modes, makes the backend signature accept xarray’s decoder kwargs, and explicitly applies CF decoding before returning the Dataset.
Breaking for users explicitly accessing ds.attrs["scale"], ds.attrs["offset"], or ds.attrs["nodata"]. These are now ds.encoding["scale_factor"], ds.encoding["add_offset"], and ds.encoding["_FillValue"] after decoding (or in ds.attrs[...] before decoding if mask_and_scale=False is passed).





Python 3.11 or newer is required. The dependency stack has moved past 3.10 (rasterix 0.2.x and current xarray both require >= 3.11), so 3.10 environments could not resolve an install at all; requires-python now states this so pip skips this release cleanly on 3.10.
Added silencing for HDF5 messages.
Chunking is delegated to xarray’s managed path (#31, closes #30). The backend no longer constructs dask collections itself: all variables open as lazy arrays, native GDAL block sizes are recorded in each data variable’s encoding["preferred_chunks"], and chunks= is applied once at the end of open_dataset via Dataset.chunk(name_prefix="gdalxarray-", token=<sha256 of the dsn>), after CF decoding and coordinate assembly. The chunked array class is therefore created by the same chunk manager xarray later uses to recognise it, which fixes “Could not find a Chunk Manager which recognises type …” errors under dask’s expression-array migration, and the explicit token means xarray only ever tokenizes strings, so the unpicklable GDAL handles are never pickled or tokenized.
Consequences: dask is now an optional dependency (install with gdalxarray[dask] or have dask present when passing chunks=); dask layer names change from gdal-multiband-{path} style to deterministic gdalxarray-{variable}-{token}; dimensions not named in an explicit chunks= mapping keep a single chunk (previously band defaulted to a chunk size of 1; chunks={} still yields per-band chunks via the recorded native block sizes); and CF decoders now always operate on lazy arrays rather than dask collections.








gdalxarray.warp() — build lazy warp-VRT recipes for reprojection, regridding, GCP/RPC/geolocation-array transformation, cutline clipping, and resampling. Returns a VRT XML string that composes with the gdalxarray engine: only the bytes the consumer reads are materialised. Common args (crs, bbox, shape, resolution, resampling, nodata) plus a full escape hatch for any gdal.WarpOptions keyword.





Classic-raster open (multidim=False) on a file with no bands but subdatasets now raises a ValueError listing the available subdataset paths and pointing at multidim=True. Previously this produced an empty 512x512 stub Dataset.








band_as_dim parameter on open_dataset (classic raster mode, default True). Bands now become an xarray band dimension on a single band_data DataArray. Pass band_as_dim=False for per-band-variable layout.
New GDALMultiBandArray BackendArray reading via dataset.ReadAsArray(band_list=...), letting GDAL handle BIP/BIL/BSQ interleaving internally.
Lazy-by-default for classic raster mode: chunks=None now returns a LazilyIndexedArray-wrapped Dataset rather than eagerly reading.
ds.encoding["source"] and ds.encoding["gdal_driver"] provenance strings (serialization-safe replacements for the live GDAL objects previously stashed in encoding).
[tool.ruff] config + .pre-commit-config.yaml for lint and format.





gdal.UseExceptions() moved from module import to GDALBackendEntrypoint.__init__, guarded with gdal.GetUseExceptions(). Scopes the side effect to actual backend use.
GDALMultiDimArray now holds optional _parent_dataset and _parent_group references internally to keep the underlying mdarray valid for the dataset’s lifetime. Previously stashed in ds.encoding, which broke to_netcdf() and other serialization paths.
Per-band metadata (description, nodata, scale, offset) in band_as_dim mode is attached as scalar attrs when uniform across bands, or as band-dim coordinates when it varies.
Multidim group navigation accepts nested paths ("/a/b/c") with tolerant leading/trailing slash handling.
Unsupported codecs on individual MDArrays (e.g. numcodecs.pcodec) are now logged at warning level and the array skipped, instead of aborting the open. This lets you open stores like Earthmover’s public ERA5 Icechunk store and access the readable coordinate/mask variables.





usable tokenize method in this frisky world
Dataset.ReadAsArray call in GDALMultiBandArray now uses xsize/ysize (the Dataset API) rather than win_xsize/win_ysize (which are the Band API).
Reverse-slice canonicalisation across all axes in all three BackendArray classes - fixes failures when xarray sends slice(stop, start, 1) for selections on decreasing coordinates (very common in atmospheric data with latitude 90 -> -90).
GDALBackendArray.__dask_tokenize__ no longer references a non-existent self.dataset attribute. Was latent (only fired on certain Dask graph hashing paths) but would have raised AttributeError when it did.
AdviseRead now skips both tiny reads (no benefit) and huge reads (which blow up on sharded stores reporting shard-sized blocks); bounded CACHE_SIZE between 4 MB and 512 MB.





Live GDAL objects no longer stored in ds.encoding. Use ds.encoding["source"] and ds.encoding["gdal_driver"] (strings) for introspection. GDAL refs are now held inside the BackendArrays themselves.








Renamed package from gdx to gdalxarray for PyPI publication. The original gdx name is taken on PyPI by an unrelated GAMS Data Exchange project.
Repository moved from mdsumner/gdx to hypertidy/gdalxarray.
Python import path is now from gdalxarray import GDALBackendEntrypoint.
Build backend switched from setuptools to hatchling; setup.py removed.
Packaging modernised to PEP 621 / PEP 639 standards.
requires-python bumped to >=3.10 to match xarray>=2025.6.





CF datetime decoding for time coordinates using units from MDArray.GetUnit() and calendar attribute.
Backend arrays accessible via ds['var'].encoding['gdal_backend'] for debugging and introspection.
GDAL dataset and group objects retained in ds.encoding['gdal_dataset'] and ds.encoding['gdal_group'] to keep MDArray methods functional.
Entry point registration so xr.open_dataset(..., engine="gdal") works.





Slice index parsing where 0 was incorrectly treated as None due to Python’s falsy evaluation (k.start or 0 -> k.start if k.start is not None else 0).
Re-enabled AdviseRead for chunk-aligned prefetching on remote datasets.





Initial release as gdx.



GDAL backend for xarray, supporting both Classic and Multidimensional APIs.
chunks={} uses native block sizes from GDAL’s GetBlockSize(), aligning Dask chunks with storage chunks for efficient reads.
multidim=True is the default for open_dataset().





Dask lazy loading for remote Zarr datasets. Zero-sized slice requests (used by Dask for _meta inference) no longer hang or attempt full array allocation.
Slice start/stop of 0 now parsed correctly.

title: BRAN2023 through kerchunk-Parquet references
text:
BRAN2023, the Bluelink ocean reanalysis (CSIRO and the Bureau of Meteorology), is daily, 0.1 degree, 51 levels, from 1993: hundreds of terabytes of netCDF on NCI’s THREDDS server. kerchunk references in Parquet describe every chunk of every file, and GDAL’s Zarr driver reads them as one store. See Byte-reference stores for what such a reference table holds.
THREDDS limits aggressive parallel reads. Eight threads is a safe cap:
dask.config.set(scheduler="threads", num_workers=8)

title: Virtual paths
text:
gdalxarray passes the string you give it to GDAL unchanged, so everything GDAL’s virtual file systems and connection strings can express is available without any code in gdalxarray. This page walks through the common ones using three days of real NOAA OISST v2.1 sea surface temperature kept with this repository, so it runs anywhere.
Data: NOAA 0.25-degree Daily Optimum Interpolation Sea Surface Temperature (OISST), Version 2.1; doi:10.25921/RE9P-PT57; licence: CC0-1.0; days 20250101, 20250102, 20250103. Built by scripts/fixtures/make_oisst.py; details in docs/fixtures/oisst/provenance.json.

title: Virtual paths
Virtual paths
section: A 2D face of an N-D array
text:
A 2D face of an N-D array
ZARR:"store":/array:i:j fixes the leading dimensions of an array to indices i, j, leaving a 2D raster that classic tools understand. Here sst is (time, zlev, lat, lon), and :2:0 picks the third day:

face = xr.open_dataset(f'ZARR:"{data(rel)}":/sst:2:0', engine="gdalxarray", multidim=False)
face["band_data"].dims, face["band_data"].shape

(('band', 'y', 'x'), (1, 720, 1440))


The stored values are identical to the multidim read of the same day:

raw_face = xr.open_dataset(f'ZARR:"{data(rel)}":/sst:2:0', engine="gdalxarray",
                           multidim=False, mask_and_scale=False)["band_data"].values[0]
raw_md = xr.open_dataset(data(rel), engine="gdalxarray",
                         mask_and_scale=False)["sst"].isel(time=2, zlev=0).values
assert np.array_equal(raw_face, raw_md)
bool(np.array_equal(raw_face, raw_md))

True


but the two models can disagree on the fill value. A Zarr v3 array has two places for one: the Zarr-level fill_value in its metadata, and a CF _FillValue among its attributes. Here is what xarray wrote for sst, OISST’s own packing being int16 with a -999 fill:

meta = data_json(f"{rel}/sst/zarr.json")
{"zarr fill_value": meta["fill_value"], "CF _FillValue": meta["attributes"].get("_FillValue")}

{'zarr fill_value': 0, 'CF _FillValue': -999}


GDAL reports the Zarr-level value as the band or array nodata; gdalxarray’s multidim path prefers the CF attribute, and the classic path has only GDAL’s band value to go on:

{"classic": face["band_data"].encoding.get("_FillValue"),
 "multidim": opened["local"]["sst"].encoding.get("_FillValue")}

{'classic': 0.0, 'multidim': -999}


So with mask-and-scale decoding on, the classic face masks 0 rather than -999: on this data, land cells (stored as -999) come through as -9.99 degrees, and real water at exactly 0 degrees is masked. Pass mask_and_scale=False and decode yourself, or prefer the multidim read, for stores written this way.

title: Virtual paths
text:
A netCDF variable, either way
One of the daily OISST netCDF files, exactly as NOAA publishes it, can be opened as a multidimensional dataset, or one variable as a classic raster with NETCDF::

nc = data("oisst/" + data_json("oisst/provenance.json")["sources"][0]["file"])
md = xr.open_dataset(nc, engine="gdalxarray")
cl = xr.open_dataset(f'NETCDF:"{nc}":sst', engine="gdalxarray", multidim=False)
md["sst"].dims, cl["band_data"].dims

(('time', 'zlev', 'lat', 'lon'), ('band', 'y', 'x'))


The two models differ in one way worth knowing: classic mode presents the raster north-up (GDAL flips a south-up netCDF to give a conventional geotransform), while multidim keeps the storage order.

fig, axs = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(10, 2.8), layout="constrained")
axs[0].imshow(md["sst"].isel(time=0, zlev=0).values, cmap="RdYlBu_r")
axs[0].set_title(f"multidim: lat[0] = {float(md.lat[0])}")
axs[1].imshow(cl["band_data"].isel(band=0).values, cmap="RdYlBu_r")
axs[1].set_title(f"classic: y[0] = {float(cl.y[0])}")
for ax in axs:
    ax.set_xticks([]); ax.set_yticks([])
plt.show()




The same netCDF variable: multidim keeps latitude ascending as stored; classic is north-up.





assert np.array_equal(md["sst"].isel(time=0, zlev=0).values[::-1],
                      cl["band_data"].isel(band=0).values, equal_nan=True)

title: Virtual paths
text:
Inline VRT options with vrt://
vrt:// wraps a source in a VRT built from URL-style options, no XML needed. A quarter-size average, and a window by coordinates:

cog = fixture("cog/world-int16-deflate.tif")
full = xr.open_dataset(cog, engine="gdalxarray", multidim=False)
small = xr.open_dataset(f"vrt://{cog}?outsize=25%,25%&r=average", engine="gdalxarray", multidim=False)
win = xr.open_dataset(f"vrt://{cog}?projwin=100,-10,160,-50", engine="gdalxarray", multidim=False)
{k: d["band_data"].shape for k, d in dict(full=full, small=small, window=win).items()}

{'full': (1, 360, 720), 'small': (1, 90, 180), 'window': (1, 80, 120)}



fig, axs = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(12, 3), layout="constrained",
                        gridspec_kw=dict(width_ratios=[2, 2, 1]))
for ax, (name, d) in zip(axs, dict(full=full, small=small, window=win).items()):
    d["band_data"].isel(band=0).plot(ax=ax, add_colorbar=False, cmap="cividis")
    ax.set_title(f"{name} {d['band_data'].shape[1:]}")

title: Guide
text:
Each page here runs against small inputs kept with the site, so it builds the same way every time, and where an input carries a GDAL oracle the page checks gdalxarray against it: if a read drifts, the site fails to build.
The inputs are moving from synthetic test stores to small cuts of real public data, each rebuilt by a script from its source with a provenance record (#41). Real so far: a Sentinel-2 scene over Hobart (open modes), three days of NOAA OISST v2.1 (virtual paths, byte-reference stores), and Antarctic sea ice with GEBCO bathymetry (warping).

Open modes

Classic rasters with bands as a dimension or as variables, and multidimensional arrays with named dimensions.

Virtual paths

Local files, /vsicurl/, ZARR: array and slice syntax, NETCDF: subdatasets and vrt:// options, all through the same call.

Byte-reference stores

A multidimensional VRT mosaic over netCDF files, the byte table behind it, and kerchunk-Parquet Zarr.

Warping

gdalxarray.warp() builds a VRT recipe; xarray opens it lazily.

Curvilinear grids

Swaths and ocean model grids placed by 2D longitude and latitude, warped by geolocation arrays.

Georeferencing conventions

Which Zarr georeferencing conventions this GDAL recognises, in each open mode, measured at build time.

title: Georeferencing conventions
text: A Zarr store can say where its cells are in several ways: CF-style 1D x/y coordinate arrays with a CRS code, the newer spatial: and proj: attribute conventions (on the group or on the array), or 2D longitude/latitude arrays. Support for each in GDAL is moving quickly, so this page measures it rather than describing it: the table below is computed from the fixtures every time the site is built.

title: Georeferencing conventions
text:
The fixtures

cases = {
    "world-int16-spatial.zarr": ("zarr/world-int16-spatial.zarr", "data",

    "polar-f32-cf.zarr": ("zarr/polar-f32-cf.zarr", "data",
                          "CF 1D x/y centres, proj:code only"),
    "utm-u16-3band-node.zarr": ("zarr/utm-u16-3band-node.zarr", "data",
                                "spatial: + proj: on the array, node registration"),
    "oisst-like.zarr": ("cf/oisst-like.zarr", "sst", "CF lat/lon, as xarray writes it"),
    "rotated.zarr": ("index/rotated.zarr", "tas", "CF rotated pole + 2D lon/lat"),

title: Georeferencing conventions
text:
What GDAL and gdalxarray see

def classic(rel, arr):
    ds = gdal.Open(f'ZARR:"{fixture(rel)}":/{arr}' + (":0" * (len(
        gdal.OpenEx(fixture(rel), gdal.OF_MULTIDIM_RASTER).GetRootGroup()
        .OpenMDArray(arr).GetDimensions()) - 2)))
    gt = ds.GetGeoTransform(can_return_null=True)
    srs = ds.GetSpatialRef()
    return gt, (srs.GetAuthorityCode(None) if srs else None)


def multidim(rel, arr):
    a = gdal.OpenEx(fixture(rel), gdal.OF_MULTIDIM_RASTER).GetRootGroup().OpenMDArray(arr)
    srs = a.GetSpatialRef()
    return srs.GetAuthorityCode(None) if srs else None


rows = []
for name, (rel, arr, how) in cases.items():
    gt, epsg_c = classic(rel, arr)
    epsg_m = multidim(rel, arr)
    t = truth.get(name)
    if t is None or gt is None:
        off = ""
    else:   # origin offset from the truth, in cells
        dx = (gt[0] - t["geotransform"][0]) / t["geotransform"][1]
        dy = (gt[3] - t["geotransform"][3]) / t["geotransform"][5]
        off = "exact" if np.allclose(gt, t["geotransform"]) else f"{dx:+.2f}, {dy:+.2f} cells"
    xds = xr.open_dataset(fixture(rel), engine="gdalxarray")
    xdims = [d for d in xds[arr].dims if d not in ("band", "time", "zlev")]
    real = all(not np.issubdtype(xds[d].dtype, np.integer) for d in xdims if d in xds.coords)
    rows.append({
        "store": name, "georeferenced by": how,
        "classic: geotransform": "yes" if gt else "no",
        "classic: vs truth": off,
        "classic: EPSG": epsg_c or "",
        "multidim: EPSG": epsg_m or "",

title: Installing gdalxarray
text:
gdalxarray is a pure-Python package and is installed with pip. It depends on the GDAL Python bindings (osgeo.gdal), which are not installable via pip alone - GDAL is a C++ library and its Python bindings need a matching system library, development headers, and a compiler.
This is the same situation faced by osgeo.gdal itself, rasterio (which sidesteps it by shipping binary wheels), and other GDAL-based tools. We recommend installing GDAL through one of the channels below, then pip install gdalxarray on top.


The fastest path to a working environment is a container that already has GDAL.


docker run --rm -it ghcr.io/hypertidy/gdal-r-python:latest bash
# inside the container:
pip install gdalxarray
This image is the reference development environment for gdalxarray. It includes GDAL 3.12+, the Python bindings, numpy 2.x, and the standard hypertidy toolchain. Tests pass here; if something works elsewhere but not here, it’s a bug.



docker run --rm -it  quay.io/pangeo/pangeo-notebook:latest bash
pip install gdalxarray
The Pangeo image is a known-working profile (verified with GDAL 3.12.3 and numpy 2.4.6) and ships JupyterLab.



For a GDAL-only base image:
docker run --rm -it ghcr.io/osgeo/gdal:ubuntu-small-latest bash

## example using venv
apt-get update && apt-get install -y python3-pip python3-venv
# --system-site-packages: the GDAL bindings live in the system Python
python3 -m venv --system-site-packages .venv
. .venv/bin/activate
pip install gdalxarray




conda-forge has well-maintained GDAL builds for Linux, macOS, and Windows.
This was tried on ubuntu.
DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get update
DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get install -y wget python3


wget https://github.com/conda-forge/miniforge/releases/latest/download/Miniforge3-Linux-x86_64.sh
## interactive step requires input
bash Miniforge3-Linux-x86_64.sh
bash
mamba create -n gdalxarray -c conda-forge python gdal numpy xarray dask
mamba activate gdalxarray
pip install gdalxarray
Or with pixi (see https://github.com/hypertidy/gdalxarray/issues/28)
A minimum-viable environment.yml:
name: gdalxarray
channels:
  - conda-forge
dependencies:
  - python>=3.11
  - gdal>=3.12
  - libgdal-netcdf
  - libgdal-hdf5
  - numpy
  - xarray>=2025.6
  - dask
  - affine
  - xproj
  - pip
  - pip:
    - gdalxarray
    - rasterix
The libgdal-* subpackages enable extra format drivers (NetCDF, HDF5). The base gdal package on conda-forge is split for size; add subpackages for the formats you need. The Zarr driver is included in the base.



If your system has a recent enough GDAL (>= 3.12), use the system package and install the Python bindings separately:
# Ubuntu / Debian
sudo apt install gdal-bin libgdal-dev python3-gdal
pip install gdalxarray

# Fedora
sudo dnf install gdal gdal-devel gdal-python3
pip install gdalxarray

# macOS (Homebrew)
brew install gdal
pip install gdal=="$(gdal-config --version).*"
pip install gdalxarray
The Homebrew path requires pip install gdal to compile against the brew GDAL, which usually works. Linux distributions ship python3-gdal precompiled.



Once GDAL is on the system, pip install gdalxarray installs only pure-Python dependencies:

numpy
xarray>=2025.6
dask (optional: only needed when opening with chunks=; install as gdalxarray[dask])
affine
rasterix
xproj

None of these need compilation.



import gdalxarray
from osgeo import gdal
print(f"gdalxarray {gdalxarray.__version__}, GDAL {gdal.__version__}")

import xarray as xr
print("gdalxarray" in xr.backends.list_engines())  # should be True

The byte table
The same three files, described chunk by chunk. The table was read from the files with GDAL (MDArray.GetRawBlockInfo) when the fixture was built, and GDAL’s Parquet driver reads it back:

def read_table(path):

    cols = [defn.GetFieldDefn(i).GetName() for i in range(defn.GetFieldCount())]

title: Byte-reference stores
text:
Decoding a chunk by hand
With a row of the table, a chunk is a range read and whatever the info column lists: here a zlib inflate and a byte unshuffle. No netCDF library is involved:

row = refs.iloc[1]
info = set(x.strip() for x in row["info"].split(";"))
print(sorted(info))

f = gdal.VSIFOpenL(data("oisst/" + row["path"]), "rb")
gdal.VSIFSeekL(f, int(row["offset"]), 0)
raw = gdal.VSIFReadL(1, int(row["size"]), f)
gdal.VSIFCloseL(f)

buf = zlib.decompress(raw) if "COMPRESSION=DEFLATE" in info else raw
itemsize = 2                                              # int16
if "FILTER=SHUFFLE" in info:                               # bytes grouped by position
    n = len(buf) // itemsize
    buf = np.frombuffer(buf, np.uint8).reshape(itemsize, n).T.copy().tobytes()
order = "<" if "ENDIANNESS=LITTLE" in info else ">"
chunk = np.frombuffer(buf, f"{order}i2").reshape(chunks)
f"{len(raw):,} bytes on disk, {chunk.nbytes:,} bytes decoded, shape {chunk.shape}"

['COMPRESSION=DEFLATE', 'ENDIANNESS=LITTLE', 'FILTER=SHUFFLE']


'667,794 bytes on disk, 2,073,600 bytes decoded, shape (1, 1, 720, 1440)'


and it matches what gdalxarray reads through the VRT, value for value:

via_gdal = xr.open_dataset(vrt, engine="gdalxarray", mask_and_scale=False)["sst"].isel(time=1).values
assert np.array_equal(chunk[0], via_gdal)
bool(np.array_equal(chunk[0], via_gdal))

True


That equality is what makes a byte table a faithful replacement for the files’ own metadata: the files can stay where they are, and the table travels.

title: Curvilinear grids
text:
Warping by geolocation arrays
To regrid a curvilinear field, GDAL’s warper can use the 2D longitude and latitude directly (“geolocation arrays”). The recipe is a VRT with a GEOLOCATION metadata domain naming the arrays; gdalxarray.warp then forwards geoloc=True to gdal.WarpOptions.
The swath fixture is 120 x 160 cells with its longitudes and latitudes as two bands of a separate file:

swath = fixture("curvilinear/swath-120x160.tif")
lonlat = fixture("curvilinear/swath-120x160-lonlat.tif")

wgs84 = osr.SpatialReference(); wgs84.ImportFromEPSG(4326)
gdal.Translate("/vsimem/swath.vrt", swath, format="VRT")
v = gdal.Open("/vsimem/swath.vrt", gdal.GA_Update)
v.SetMetadata({"X_DATASET": lonlat, "X_BAND": "1", "Y_DATASET": lonlat, "Y_BAND": "2",
               "PIXEL_OFFSET": "0", "LINE_OFFSET": "0", "PIXEL_STEP": "1", "LINE_STEP": "1",
               "SRS": wgs84.ExportToWkt(), "GEOREFERENCING_CONVENTION": "PIXEL_CENTER"},
              "GEOLOCATION")
v = None

The fixture manifest gives target grids; one in Antarctic Polar Stereographic:

man = fixture_json("curvilinear/manifest.json")
case = next(c for c in man["cases"] if c["name"] == "swath-to-3031")
gt, W, H = case["geotransform"], case["width"], case["height"]
bbox = (gt[0], gt[3] + gt[5] * H, gt[0] + gt[1] * W, gt[3])

ll = xr.open_dataset(lonlat, engine="gdalxarray", multidim=False)["band_data"]
raw = xr.open_dataset(swath, engine="gdalxarray", multidim=False)["band_data"].isel(band=0)
warped = {m: xr.open_dataset(gdalxarray.warp("/vsimem/swath.vrt", crs=case["crs"], bbox=bbox,
                                             shape=(W, H), resampling=m, geoloc=True,
                                             nodata=-9999,
                                             errorThreshold=man["error_threshold"]),
                             engine="gdalxarray", multidim=False)["band_data"].isel(band=0)
          for m in ["near", "bilinear"]}


fig, axs = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(13, 4), layout="constrained")
raw.plot(ax=axs[0], cmap="viridis", add_colorbar=False); axs[0].set_title("index space")
axs[1].pcolormesh(ll.isel(band=0), ll.isel(band=1), raw, cmap="viridis", shading="nearest")
axs[1].set_title("lon, lat"); axs[1].set_aspect(1 / np.cos(np.radians(-44)))
warped["bilinear"].plot(ax=axs[2], cmap="viridis", add_colorbar=False)
axs[2].set_aspect("equal"); axs[2].set_title("EPSG:3031, bilinear")
plt.show()




The swath in index space, its own longitude/latitude, and warped to EPSG:3031 by its geolocation arrays.




As on the Warping page, gdalxarray must match GDAL’s own read of the same recipe exactly; the fixture’s pinned oracle is reported:

rows = []
for r in case["results"]:
    if r["resampling"] not in warped:
        continue
    vrt = gdalxarray.warp("/vsimem/swath.vrt", crs=case["crs"], bbox=bbox, shape=(W, H),
                          resampling=r["resampling"], geoloc=True,
                          errorThreshold=man["error_threshold"])
    gx = xr.open_dataset(vrt, engine="gdalxarray", multidim=False,
                         mask_and_scale=False)["band_data"].values[0]
    ref = gdal.Open(vrt).ReadAsArray()
    pin = fixture_array("curvilinear/" + r["file"], "float32").reshape(H, W)
    eq = lambda a, b: float(np.mean((a == b) | (np.isnan(a) & np.isnan(b))))
    rows.append((r["resampling"], eq(gx, ref), eq(ref, pin)))
    assert np.array_equal(gx, ref, equal_nan=True)

title: Warping
text:
Checked against GDAL
scripts/fixtures/make_warp.py defines target grids over these two sources (lon/lat, WGS84 polar stereographic, Equal Earth, orthographic, and two coarse cases where GDAL reads an overview) and records what gdal.Warp writes for each: into memory, single-threaded, error threshold 0.125. For each case this page compares:

gdalxarray: gdalxarray.warp() opened with xarray;
GDAL VRT: the same warped VRT read by GDAL itself (gdal.Warp(format="VRT") then ReadAsArray);
GDAL direct: gdal.Warp into memory with the same settings as the recorded case, using the GDAL this page was built with;
pinned: the recorded result, from the GDAL version in the manifest.

gdalxarray must agree with the GDAL VRT on every cell: that is the claim this package makes, that it adds nothing to what GDAL reads. The other two columns are reported, not required. A warped VRT computes each block on its own, so where the approximate transformer struggles (near a pole, say) it can differ from a single direct warp; and GDAL’s resampling kernels can change between releases.

def same(a, b):
    return float(np.mean((a == b) | (np.isnan(a) & np.isnan(b)))) if a.dtype.kind == "f" \
        else float(np.mean(a == b))

    bbox = (gt[0], gt[3] + gt[5] * H, gt[0] + gt[1] * W, gt[3])
    pinned_all = np.load(data("warp/" + c["file"]))
    for m in c["resampling"]:
        kw = dict(crs=c["crs"], bbox=bbox, shape=(W, H), resampling=m,
                  errorThreshold=c["error_threshold"])
        if c["overview"] == "none":

        vrt = gdalxarray.warp(data(c["source"]), **kw)
        gx = xr.open_dataset(vrt, engine="gdalxarray", multidim=False,
                             mask_and_scale=False)["band_data"].values[0]
        vrt_gdal = gdal.Open(vrt).ReadAsArray()
        direct = warp_direct(data(c["source"]), c["crs"], gt, W, H, m, c["overview"])
        rows.append({"case": c["name"], "resampling": m,
                     "gdalxarray = GDAL VRT": same(gx, vrt_gdal),
                     "GDAL VRT = GDAL direct": same(vrt_gdal, direct),
                     "GDAL direct = pinned": same(direct, pinned_all[m])})

title: Copernicus Marine ARCO Zarr
text:
Copernicus Marine serves its products as Zarr v2 with consolidated metadata on an S3-compatible endpoint, twice over: timeChunked.zarr (one time step, a large spatial block per chunk: good for maps) and geoChunked.zarr (many time steps, a small spatial block: good for time series). The buckets refuse listing, which does not matter: the ZARR: prefix tells GDAL what it is looking at, and GDAL goes from .zmetadata to chunk keys by the Zarr spec.
The store URLs are versioned by dataset (_202411, _202311, …), and Copernicus retires old versions, so these addresses are stable until the next version of each product.

title: warp
text:
warp
Lazy warp-VRT recipe construction.
The :func:warp function builds a description of a warp operation — target CRS, resolution, bounds, GCP/RPC/geoloc transformer, cutline, etc. — and returns it as VRT XML text. The result composes with :class:GDALBackendEntrypoint::
>>> import gdalxarray
>>> import xarray as xr
>>> vrt = gdalxarray.warp(source, crs="+proj=laea")
>>> ds = xr.open_dataset(vrt, engine="gdalxarray", multidim=False)
No pixels are read or written by warp() — the VRT is a recipe. Bytes flow only when the consumer (xarray, gdalwarp, gdal_translate) asks for a window.





Name
Description




warp
Build a warped-VRT recipe string.





warp.warp(
    source,
    *,
    crs=None,
    bbox=None,
    shape=None,
    resolution=None,
    resampling='near',
    nodata=None,
    src_nodata=None,
    bands=None,
    **warp_options,
)
Build a warped-VRT recipe string.
Wraps :func:gdal.Warp with format="VRT" to produce a textual description of a reprojection / regrid / warp. The result is a self-contained VRT XML string that downstream tools can read lazily.
The named keyword arguments cover the common cases. Any further :func:gdal.WarpOptions keyword can be passed as an additional keyword argument and is forwarded verbatim — see GDAL’s gdal.WarpOptions documentation for the full list (transformer options for RPC/GCPs/geolocation arrays, cutlines, alpha-band handling, working type, etc.).











Name
Type
Description
Default




source
str
GDAL-recognised source path or URI. Anything gdal.Open can handle: local file, /vsicurl/, /vsis3/, vrt://, ZARR:"...", NETCDF:...:var, etc.
required


crs
str or int
Target CRS as PROJ string, WKT, or EPSG code. Maps to GDAL’s dstSRS.
None


bbox
sequence of 4 floats
Output bounding box (xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax) in target CRS units. Maps to GDAL’s outputBounds.
None


shape
tuple of 2 ints
Output (width, height) in pixels. Maps to GDAL’s width and height.
None


resolution
float or tuple of 2 floats
Output resolution. A scalar means isotropic (res, res). A tuple is (xres, yres). Maps to GDAL’s xRes / yRes.
None


resampling
str
Resampling algorithm: "near", "bilinear", "cubic", "cubicspline", "lanczos", "average", "mode", "min", "max", "med", "q1", "q3", "sum", "rms". Maps to GDAL’s resampleAlg.
"near"


nodata
float
Output nodata value. Maps to GDAL’s dstNodata.
None


src_nodata
float
Override the source nodata value. Maps to GDAL’s srcNodata.
None


bands
list of int
Subset of source bands to warp (1-based). Maps to GDAL’s srcBands.
None


**warp_options

Any other keyword argument is forwarded to :func:gdal.WarpOptions verbatim. Common power-user options: rpc=True, tps=True, geoloc=True, transformerOptions=[...], cutlineWKT="POLYGON(...)", cropToCutline=True, coordinateOperation="+proj=...".
{}














Name
Type
Description





str
VRT XML describing the warped output. Suitable for xr.open_dataset(..., engine="gdalxarray"), for any GDAL tool that accepts a path, or for writing to a .vrt file as a portable, durable warp recipe.






Runtime-only options (multithread, warpMemoryLimit, creationOptions, callback, callback_data) are not serialised into the VRT description — they affect how a warp is executed, not what the warp produces. Passing them to warp() emits a :class:UserWarning and they are dropped. To control runtime behaviour for the eventual read, set GDAL config options on the consumer side, e.g.::
gdal.SetConfigOption("GDAL_NUM_THREADS", "4")
ds = xr.open_dataset(vrt, engine="gdalxarray")



Reproject anything to Lambert Azimuthal Equal Area, lazily::
vrt = warp(src, crs="+proj=laea")
ds = xr.open_dataset(vrt, engine="gdalxarray", multidim=False)
Specific target grid::
vrt = warp(
    src,
    crs="EPSG:3577",
    bbox=(-2000000, -5000000, 2000000, -1000000),
    resolution=1000,
    resampling="bilinear",
)
Drone imagery with GCPs, warped via thin-plate splines::
vrt = warp(src, crs="EPSG:32755", tps=True)
Satellite Level-1B product with RPCs and a DEM::
vrt = warp(
    src,
    crs="EPSG:4326",
    rpc=True,
    transformerOptions=["RPC_DEM=/path/to/dem.tif"],
)
